A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MetaSym and retain matching core methods and experiments. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original prediction experiments on simulated spring-mesh, quantum and quadrotor systems, including benchmark scores and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds real-data quadrotor predictions, harmonic-oscillator experiments and further empirical analyses.

M1.justification: The LA-SympNet encoder, bidirectional loss, frozen-encoder decoder training, query/value adaptation and autoregressive inference are retained. V3 expands the symmetry and MAML explanations without establishing a changed algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: V3 retains the simulated domains and adds evaluation on real-world quadrotor data, substantially extending coverage beyond simulation (Section 4.3, Figure 4). Appendix D.1.2 also adds a separately trained and tested harmonic-oscillator family.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Dissipative SymODEN for spring-mesh and quadrotor systems, and FNO and iMODE across all three domains. Appendix D.3 adds conventional ActiveDecoder fine-tuning as a comparator. QuantumLSTM was already evaluated in v2 and is renamed QLSTM.

E3.justification: V3 extends evaluation with a context-window sweep from 2 to 100 steps and oscillator energy/phase-space-area measurements against analytical trajectories. Existing benchmark hyperparameters are largely retained. The new blanket 30-step statement in Appendix E conflicts with the quadrotor table's retained value of 10, leaving that setting unresolved.

E4.justification: V3 adds direct oscillator conservation tests, quantum-ensemble analysis, comparison against conventional fine-tuning, query/value adaptation heatmaps and context-window sensitivity analysis. These substantially broaden the diagnostic evidence. The conservative spring-mesh experiment and empirical perturbation-bound analysis remain.

E5.justification: V3 Figure 5 newly specifies a quantum-trajectory ensemble of 100 simulation runs and displays a ±1σ band labelled a confidence interval. Existing benchmark MSE±σ reporting is retained; an increase in repeated model-training runs is not established.

E6.justification: Shared Table 1 scores are unchanged. V3 adds comparator results, real-quadrotor MSE of 0.028±0.091 across 54 trajectories, oscillator areas of 21.602 versus 21.619, context-window results and 1.551 ms inference timing. The real-data score is not directly comparable to the retained simulated-quadrotor score.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds an explicit shear-update Jacobian and the symmetric cross-derivative condition for symplecticity. Appendix D.1.2 adds oscillator equations, their analytical solution and phase-area reasoning. The near-symplectic composition theorem and proof in Appendix C are retained despite renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion now claim demonstrated adaptation on real-world quadrotor data and robustness to actual sensor noise. The central structure-preservation, compact-model, few-shot generalization and classical/quantum novelty claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 newly qualifies its strongest guarantees as depending on representative conservative pretraining data and weakening without it. It also adds interpretations of conservation results, adaptation through informative gradients, and the tradeoff between prediction horizon and accuracy.

D1.justification: Appendix G newly discloses 80/20 training/validation and 30/70 decoder adaptation/inference splits. V3 also clarifies unweighted MSE aggregation, documents symmetric encoder constructions and supplies oscillator-generation parameters. These additions do not establish changes to previously undisclosed settings.

R1.justification: V3 adds positioning against Meta-PINNs and physics-informed operator learning, emphasizing architectural constraints versus loss penalties (Conclusion; Penwarden et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2021). Additional citations support the real-data benchmark and adaptation/oscillator discussions; the main related-work narrative remains.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain. V3 expands the MAML explanation, subdivides conservative-system analyses, adds a context-window appendix, updates author/publication text and revises discussion. The main-text proof sketch is removed while the full appendix proof remains.

P2.justification: V3 adopts the TMLR layout with a redesigned author block and headers, expands tables, and adds real-quadrotor, quantum-ensemble, oscillator and adaptation-heatmap figures. The simulated quadrotor plot moves from v2 Figure 4 to appendix Figure 6, while adaptation Figure 5 becomes Figure 8.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens validation by extending v2's simulation-only evaluation to real quadrotor data, testing relevant additional competitors, and directly examining energy and phase-area preservation. These address important gaps in support for practical transfer and physical consistency. Limited real-data protocol detail and inconsistent context-window reporting remain, but the gains in diagnostic evidence are substantial.
